title: Deep full-project result-weakness audit and improvement diagnosis (UNSW-NB15 hierarchical Head 2)
commands_run: READ-ONLY content search (ripgrep) for stale '\b190\b' references across the repo
READ-ONLY file globs to enumerate results/final/hierarchical/** and results/audits/unsw_*
All other inspection was direct file reads (no code, training, preprocessing, or eval execution)

a9_6_recap.outcome: FAILED as a Head 2 improvement: binary improved, attack-family macro-F1 and rare-class macro-F1 declined, attack FN rose.

no_bug_verifications: Label/taxonomy mapping consistent: attack_family_label_mapping id_to_class (Generic0..Worms8) matches per_class_attack_metrics.csv class_id order and the confusion-matrix column order. No off-by-one.
split_summary.json per-class supports exactly match test_metrics.json per-class supports (e.g. Generic 18871, Analysis 677, Worms 44). No label drift.
Mask integrity verified in split_summary for all splits: y_attack_family == -1 exactly where mask == 0; mask_0_count == benign count; attack rows carry valid 0..8 labels.
Loss masking correct: Head 2 CrossEntropy is applied only to (mask==1 & y_attack!=ignore); benign rows excluded; all-benign batch returns a zero attack-loss tensor (no NaN).

Class-weight wiring correct: pos_weight applied to BCEWithLogits (Head 1); attack_class_weights applied to F.cross_entropy(weight=...) (Head 2), length-validated == attack_head_dim, ordered by class id.
attack_loss_weight genuinely scales the Head 2 term in total_loss; A9.6 truly used 1.5 (verified in config and trainer).
Metric computation not inflated: multiclass macro-F1 is over the FULL fixed 9-class set, so never-predicted classes correctly score 0 and drag the macro down.

Head 2 macro-F1 is evaluated on attack rows only (teacher-forced, Head-1-independent); the routed end-to-end view (0.7208 of attacks correctly attributed) is slightly harsher, so the 0.50 headline is not optimistic relative to deployment.
Binary macro-F1 0.894488 reconstructs exactly from the confusion matrix (benign-F1 0.8789, attack-F1 0.9101, mean 0.8945). Not inflated.
Class weights computed from train labels only (validation/test labels never read); no test-set tuning; checkpoint selected by validation only.

high_findings.title: Intrinsic feature-space overlap of Analysis / Backdoor / DoS (and partly Exploits)
high_findings.evidence: Confusion matrix: true Analysis -> DoS 479/677 and -> Backdoor 109/677 (only 5 correct); true Backdoor -> DoS 409/583 (95 correct); true DoS -> Exploits 1039 and -> Backdoor 775 (1973 correct). These four families form one mutually-confused cluster.
high_findings.expected_impact: Dominant limiter of attack-family macro-F1. Analysis F1 0.0123 and Backdoor F1 0.0704 alone hold the 9-class macro near 0.50.
high_findings.fix_idea: Largely not fixable by tuning; it is a UNSW label/feature property. Manage with realistic targets, optional super-class reporting head, and modest feature engineering. Do NOT promise separation that the data does not support.

high_findings.title: Severe imbalance and tiny absolute support for rare/hard families
high_findings.evidence: Train attack-row support: Worms 109, Shellcode 965, Backdoor 1505, Analysis 1675 vs Generic 33959 / Exploits 28482. Worms = 0.107% of attack rows. Rare-class precision is low (Shellcode 0.308, Worms 0.221, Backdoor 0.045) while recall is high -> class weighting buys recall at precision cost.
high_findings.expected_impact: High variance and low precision on minority families; drags macro-F1; also makes single-seed comparisons noisy.
high_findings.fix_idea: Target precision repair (class-weight cap/temperature) rather than more recall pressure; report multi-seed mean+/-std for these classes.

medium_findings.title: Head 2 is a single linear layer over a binary-dominated shared embedding
medium_findings.evidence: Model code: attack_head = nn.Linear(128, 9) with no dedicated non-linear branch. Binary objective is near-saturated (train_binary_loss 0.077, val_binary_macro_f1 ~0.93 and flat) while train_attack_loss is far higher (0.69) and val attack macro-F1 plateaus ~0.59. The shared 128-d embedding is shaped mostly by the easy binary task.
medium_findings.expected_impact: Limits Head 2 capacity to carve non-linear family boundaries out of the overlapping cluster. Most actionable structural lever.
medium_findings.fix_idea: Add a dedicated 2-layer non-linear Head 2 branch (e.g. 128->128->9, GELU+dropout) while keeping the loss/weights/optimizer/protocol identical. One controlled factor (head depth). Avoids A9.6's failure mode (no extra minority loss pressure).

medium_findings.title: Official UNSW partition prior shift inflates binary FP on test and the val->test gap
medium_findings.evidence: Train+val benign fraction = 56000/175341 = 31.9% vs test benign fraction = 37000/82332 = 44.9%. Validation benign FP rate 0.0549 jumps to test 0.1672; val binary macro-F1 0.933 -> test 0.894; val attack macro-F1 0.592 -> test 0.500. This is the known official-protocol covariate/prior shift, not a bug.
medium_findings.expected_impact: Binary precision/FP penalty on test; part of the honest val->test gap. It is a property of the corrected benchmark protocol.
medium_findings.fix_idea: Optional: validation-only decision-threshold calibration to trade FP/FN (benefit is bounded because val and test priors also differ). Report the gap explicitly; do not tune on test.

medium_findings.title: Global attack_loss_weight is a blunt lever; more minority pressure lowers rare precision without separating Analysis/Backdoor
medium_findings.evidence: A9.6 (weight 1.5) dropped Shellcode precision 0.308->0.236, DoS F1 0.388->0.338, macro-F1 0.500->0.485; Analysis/Backdoor stayed on the floor. Increasing global Head 2 pressure pushed more over-prediction of already-recalled minorities.
medium_findings.expected_impact: Explains why A9.6 failed and warns that focal-loss-with-class-weights (another minority/hard-pressure lever) risks the same precision-collapse pattern.
medium_findings.fix_idea: Prefer capacity (RC3) and precision repair over more minority loss pressure. If focal loss is tried, gate strictly on rare-class precision floors.

medium_findings.title: Single-seed experiment comparisons are within run-to-run noise
medium_findings.evidence: Validation attack macro-F1 swings ~+/-0.02-0.03 epoch-to-epoch within each run; A9 vs A9.6 differ by only 0.014951 macro-F1 with N=1 seed each. A 0.01-0.02 difference cannot be distinguished from noise.
medium_findings.expected_impact: Risk of over-interpreting noise as signal; weakens the rigor of promote/reject decisions.
medium_findings.fix_idea: Run every future experiment with >=3 seeds and report mean+/-std for the headline and rare-class metrics. Promote only on differences beyond the observed noise band.

low_findings.title: Feature space is 69% ultra-rare protocol one-hots, standard-scaled
low_findings.evidence: feature_names.json: 133/192 features are proto_* one-hot dummies (most ultra-rare, e.g. proto_aris, proto_aes-sp3-d), 13 service + 7 state + 39 numeric. One-hot columns are StandardScaler-scaled, amplifying rare-category spikes.
low_findings.expected_impact: Low-medium noise dilution; unlikely to be the dominant limiter because the easy classes (Generic 0.98, Recon 0.82) already score well with the same features.
low_findings.fix_idea: Later experiment: prune ultra-rare proto dummies / frequency-encode proto / leave one-hots unscaled. Changes feature_dim (breaks direct comparability) and needs careful re-preprocessing.

low_findings.title: No LR scheduler / no gradient clipping; constant LR 0.001; training hit max_epochs not early stop
low_findings.evidence: training_history.csv: learning_rate constant 0.001 for all 40 epochs; best epoch 35, ran to max 40 (patience 6 not triggered). Val attack macro-F1 had effectively plateaued by epoch ~19-25.
low_findings.expected_impact: Low. A cosine/step LR could marginally stabilize the plateau; longer training is unlikely to raise the ceiling.
low_findings.fix_idea: Optional cosine LR decay; low priority.

low_findings.title: No class-balanced sampler for attack rows (Worms <1 sample/batch)
low_findings.evidence: batch_size 1024 over 149039 train rows -> ~0.75 Worms and ~6.6 Shellcode per batch. But rare recall is already high (Shellcode 0.77, Worms 0.66); the problem is precision, which a balanced sampler would not fix and could worsen.
low_findings.expected_impact: Low / possibly negative for macro-F1. Not recommended as a lever.
low_findings.fix_idea: Do not pursue balanced/oversampling for macro-F1; project policy already disables oversampling.

low_findings.title: Validation objective weights binary 50% though binary is near-saturated
low_findings.evidence: val_binary_macro_f1 span ~0.013 vs val_attack_family_macro_f1 span ~0.12 across epochs. The 0.5/0.5 blend lets a near-flat binary term occupy half the selection signal.
low_findings.expected_impact: Low. Selection-only; cannot exceed the best attack-F1 epoch actually produced (bounded by the plateau).
low_findings.fix_idea: Cheap companion experiment: reweight selection to 0.3*binary + 0.7*attack to bias toward better Head 2 epochs.

low_findings.title: Stale '190' references in README, two dimension-agnostic smoke tests, and pytest cache
low_findings.evidence: README.md:46 still says UNSW '190'; tests/test_hierarchical_advanced_model.py uses input_dim=190 in synthetic forward smoke tests (model is dimension-agnostic, so tests still valid); .pytest_cache holds stale node ids. Active hierarchical training/preprocessing path correctly uses 192 (config, hierarchical_config.py, hierarchical_validation.py, and the trained artifacts all show 192).
low_findings.expected_impact: None on A9 results. Legacy binary/FedAvg configs intentionally keep 190 (documented in docs/UNSW_SPLIT_PROTOCOL_DECISION.md).
low_findings.fix_idea: Out of scope for this no-edit task; note for a later documentation pass.

likely_root_causes: RC1 intrinsic Analysis/Backdoor/DoS/Exploits feature-space overlap (dominant macro-F1 limiter)
RC2 severe imbalance / tiny absolute support for rare-hard families (low minority precision)
RC3 single-linear Head 2 over a binary-dominated shared embedding (most actionable structural lever)
RC4 official-partition prior shift (binary FP + val->test gap; intrinsic to the corrected protocol)
RC5 global attack_loss_weight is too blunt; more minority pressure hurt precision (explains A9.6)
focal_loss_assessment: Credible but NOT the clearly-best next step and NOT my primary recommendation. Focal loss combined with the existing class weights is another minority/hard-pressure lever, and the A9.6 evidence (RC5) shows added minority pressure lowered rare-class precision while leaving Analysis/Backdoor on the floor. Focal loss can reweight the loss landscape but cannot separate families that overlap in feature space (RC1). If run, it must be strictly gated on rare-class precision floors and reported across >=3 seeds.

next_experiment_recommendation.primary: A9.7 head2_branch_capacity: add a dedicated 2-layer non-linear Head 2 branch (e.g. 128->128->9, GELU + dropout) while keeping CrossEntropy, train-only class weights, attack_loss_weight=1.0, optimizer, LR, threshold, validation objective, and the corrected UNSW protocol unchanged. One controlled factor (Head 2 depth). Directly targets RC3 and avoids the A9.6 minority-pressure failure mode.
next_experiment_recommendation.cheap_companion: A9.8 selection_objective_reweight: change only the validation selection blend to 0.3*binary + 0.7*attack_family macro-F1 (selection-only, zero training-dynamics change).
next_experiment_recommendation.precision_repair_option: A9.9 attack_weight_cap_down: reduce the attack class-weight cap/temperature to lift rare-class precision (opposite direction to A9.6).
next_experiment_recommendation.demoted_option: head2_focal_loss (the prior A9.6-review recommendation): keep as a later, precision-gated alternative, not the next step.
next_experiment_recommendation.must_use_methodology: >=3 seeds with mean+/-std; keep A9 as the frozen baseline; separate output paths; promote only on differences beyond the noise band and the existing success gates; never select or tune on the test split.

expected_realistic_improvement.qualitative_goal: Lift at least one of Analysis / Backdoor / DoS off the floor without collapsing Shellcode/Worms precision.

why_above_0_9_unrealistic: On the corrected official UNSW-NB15 split, Analysis/Backdoor/DoS/Exploits overlap by construction; published 9-class work routinely reports near-zero Analysis/Backdoor F1 and macro-F1 in the ~0.45-0.60 band (high weighted-F1 ~0.75-0.80 is dominated by Generic/Exploits). A macro-F1 > 0.9 would require near-perfect separation of intrinsically-entangled families and is not achievable from these features without changing the problem (e.g. merging families or adding richer data).
